stem: A canopy map has readings of 900, 880, 860, 520, 500, and 490 µmol·m⁻²·s⁻¹. What does the map reveal that a single center reading near 900 would miss?
choices: The canopy has substantial spatial nonuniformity
The photoperiod may be mismatched because lower readings usually indicate areas receiving fewer hours of effective light
The fixture spectrum may be uneven across the canopy because PPFD differences directly identify changes in spectral composition
The daily light integral should be treated as equivalent at every point if the center measurement remains close to 900 µmol·m⁻²·s⁻¹
rationale: The spread from roughly 490 to 900 µmol·m⁻²·s⁻¹ shows major spatial variation. A single high center reading would hide lower-light areas.
